From 9f60aeaced0c4dc50b668bbf4d4a9c8472283c71 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Nitin Gupta <ngupta@vflare.org>
Date: Wed, 2 Jan 2013 08:53:41 -0800
Subject: [PATCH] staging: zram: fix invalid memory references during disk
 write

(cherry pick from commit 397c60668aa5ae7130b5ad4e73870d7b8a787085)

Fixes a bug introduced by commit c8f2f0db1 ("zram: Fix handling
of incompressible pages") which caused invalid memory references
during disk write. Invalid references could occur in two cases:
 - Incoming data expands on compression: In this case, reference was
made to kunmap()'ed bio page.
 - Partial (non PAGE_SIZE) write with incompressible data: In this
case, reference was made to a kfree()'ed buffer.

Fixes bug 50081:
https://bugzilla.kernel.org/show_bug.cgi?id=50081

Signed-off-by: Nitin Gupta <ngupta@vflare.org>
Cc: stable <stable@vger.kernel.org>
Reported-by: Mihail Kasadjikov <hamer.mk@gmail.com>
Reported-by: Tomas M <tomas@slax.org>
Reviewed-by: Minchan Kim <minchan@kernel.org>
Signed-off-by: Greg Kroah-Hartman <gregkh@linuxfoundation.org>
Bug: 24810447
Change-Id: Ia6558c1f89896522679f99472d801b1060dc3628

diff --git a/drivers/staging/zram/zram_drv.c b/drivers/staging/zram/zram_drv.c
index e34e3fe0ae2..34e0edb70b2 100644
--- a/drivers/staging/zram/zram_drv.c
+++ b/drivers/staging/zram/zram_drv.c
@@ -271,9 +271,8 @@ static int zram_bvec_write(struct zram *zram, struct bio_vec *bvec, u32 index,
 	}
 
 	if (page_zero_filled(uncmem)) {
-		kunmap_atomic(user_mem);
-		if (is_partial_io(bvec))
-			kfree(uncmem);
+		if (!is_partial_io(bvec))
+			kunmap_atomic(user_mem);
 		zram->stats.pages_zero++;
 		zram_set_flag(meta, index, ZRAM_ZERO);
 		ret = 0;
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `drivers/staging/zram/zram_drv.c`**
   - The code block within the `zram_bvec_write` function has been modified to change the order of operations related to memory management.
   - The `kunmap_atomic(user_mem)` call has been moved to only execute if the I/O operation is not partial (`!is_partial_io(bvec)`), preventing it from being called when the operation is partial.
   - The `kfree(uncmem)` call has been removed from the conditional block that checks for `is_partial_io(bvec)`, which prevents a potential invalid memory reference when dealing with incompressible data.

### Relationships Between Modifications

- The changes made in `zram_drv.c` directly address the issues caused by the previous commit (`c8f2f0db1`), which introduced bugs related to invalid memory references during disk writes. 
- By ensuring that `kunmap_atomic(user_mem)` is only called when the I/O operation is complete (not partial), the patch prevents dereferencing a memory page that has already been unmapped, thus fixing the invalid memory reference issue.
- Additionally, by removing the `kfree(uncmem)` call from the partial I/O condition, the patch avoids referencing a buffer that may have already been freed, further mitigating the risk of invalid memory access. 
- Overall, these modifications enhance the stability and reliability of the zram driver during disk write operations, particularly in handling edge cases involving incompressible data.

This could lead to an attempt to unmap a memory page that has already been unmapped, as indicated by the root cause of the bug. Reason: The provided code snippet contains a potential bug because it calls `kunmap_atomic(user_mem)` unconditionally within the `if (is_partial_io(bvec))` block. If `is_partial_io(bvec)` returns true, it attempts to unmap `user_mem` after it has been used in a `memcpy`, which could lead to accessing an unmapped page. Additionally, the second call to `kunmap_atomic(user_mem)` in the `if (!is_partial_io(bvec))` block is also problematic because it may be called when `user_mem` is already unmapped or invalid, especially since `user_mem` is set to `NULL` after the first unmap. This violates the fix's condition of ensuring that `kunmap_atomic(user_mem)` is only called when it is safe to do so.
